lines.text: I started this part of the trip by finding a quiet corner to settle into.
In the rented flat, small details made the room feel like a place of its own.
A lamp, books, games, and a plant filled the frame around me.
Then I got to my feet and took in the room from another angle.
The poster on the wall carried a holiday theme that stayed with me.
For a moment, the flat became my base between days out.
On the Royal Mile, I paused outside Old Town Chambers with my companion.
The entrance, flowers, and bicycles gave this stop its own street scene.
We shared a moment here, surrounded by the color of the flower bed.
Inside St Giles’, I walked into the nave and looked up.
The long view drew me forward, toward the blue vaulted chancel.
I let my eyes follow the height and detail above me.
At the far end, a stained-glass window rises above two paintings.
The window inscription names Sir James Falshaw and dates from the eighteen-seventies. [FACT TO VERIFY]
The paintings below appear to be signed Bellany; I’m checking the attribution. [FACT TO VERIFY]
I turned toward the paintings and took a closer look.
Above them, the colored glass holds its own stories in the light.
I followed the window upward, then carried that image with me.
Later, by the Thames in London, the city lights framed the night.
The skyline included the Walkie-Talkie, its shape clear among the buildings. [FACT TO VERIFY]
After Edinburgh, this riverside view marked another city in the trip.
I looked out across the water and let the journey settle into night.
